_metadata.independence: I read only u18-blind-input.json and no other file, repository content, web page or API.

hints.reason: A lantern is a flame (fire) enclosed in a glass housing, one familiar object reaching both words.
Glass is blown (glassblowing) strongly, but fire is only reached via blowing a flame out or stoking it, a thin verb link.
A furnace holds fire, and glass is melted and worked in a glass furnace.

best_available.why: A single everyday object that is literally fire inside glass.

pairs.pair_note: Two clean hints; BLOWN leans on glass alone.

hints.reason: A forge is a fire for working metal; gold is forged by goldsmiths, though iron is the more typical forge metal.
Gold is refined, and the familiar phrase 'refined by fire' / 'refiner's fire' supplies the fire side.
Fire melts things and melting gold is a familiar scene (gold bars, molten gold).

best_available.why: Shared verb that is vivid for both words without needing a phrase.

pairs.pair_note: All three pass; MELT is the broadest.

hints.reason: Beeswax sits beside honey in the hive, and wax burns as candle fuel, reaching fire via candles.
Bees make honey, but there is no recognizable bee route to fire.
Smoke comes from fire, and beekeepers smoke the hive to calm bees when harvesting honey.

best_available.why: The beekeeper's smoker is a recognizable scene and fire is immediate.

pairs.pair_note: A hard pair; both passes need a hop on one side. BEE is pure filler on the fire side.

hints.reason: Game of Thrones is the adaptation of 'A Song of Ice and Fire', naming both words.
Fire and ice are a classic pair of opposites; the hint points at the relationship between the two targets.
Frost is ice, and the fire side only arrives through Robert Frost's poem 'Fire and Ice', which few players will reach.

best_available.why: Both words are literally in the source title.

pairs.pair_note: THRONES is excellent; FROST is clever but one-sided in practice.

hints.reason: You strike a match or flint to make fire, and you strike a key on a keyboard or piano.
Ignition is the start of fire, and the ignition key starts a car.
Fire escape and the Escape key are both familiar compounds.

best_available.why: Two everyday compounds, zero explanation needed.

pairs.pair_note: A model pair; all three are strong.

hints.reason: Contains the target FIRE as a substring (rule failure); the king side is also absent.
Burger King is the brand, and burgers are flame-grilled over fire (that chain's own slogan).
Dragons breathe fire, but the king side is only a loose fantasy association (Dragon King), not a specific scene.

best_available.why: Brand route to king plus the flame-grill image for fire.

pairs.pair_note: FIRED is a rule failure. BURGER is the only servable hint.

hints.reason: A torch is fire; the knight side is only a generic medieval-castle image with no specific knight-and-torch scene.
Dragons breathe fire and knights slay dragons (St George), a shared story.
A forge is fire, and a knight's sword and armor come from the forge.

best_available.why: The knight-versus-dragon story is universally known and fire is intrinsic to it.

pairs.pair_note: DRAGON is excellent here; TORCH is mostly fire.

hints.reason: A mane is the lion's defining feature, but there is no recognizable mane route to fire beyond poetic 'fiery mane'.
The circus has lion tamers and fire-eaters/flaming hoops, one shared scene.
Leo is the lion sign of the zodiac and is one of the fire signs.

best_available.why: Lion tamer and fire act in one tent.

pairs.pair_note: MANE is one-sided filler; the other two are good.

hints.reason: A lantern holds a flame; the moon side relies on the moon-as-lantern poetic image or Mid-Autumn lantern festivals, which most players will not reach.
Rockets fly to the moon on a tail of fire.
'Ring of Fire' is a familiar phrase and a ring around the moon (halo) is a known sight.

best_available.why: Fire at one end, moon at the other, one picture.

pairs.pair_note: ROCKET is ideal; LANTERN does not reach the moon for most players.

hints.reason: Smoke is fire's companion but has no recognizable mouse connection.
A wired computer mouse (and mice chewing wires) gives the mouse side; faulty wiring starting fires gives the fire side.

best_available.why: The only hint that touches both words.

pairs.pair_note: Hard pair; WIRE is adequate, SMOKE is filler.

hints.reason: Contains the target FIRE as a substring (rule failure), though Bonfire Night would otherwise fit both.
Contains the target FIRE as a substring (rule failure).
Fire glows, and a glow is something seen against the dark of night.
Campfire is the compound, and camping around the fire is a night scene.

best_available.why: Campfire at night is one shared picture.

pairs.pair_note: Two rule failures; CAMP and GLOW remain servable.

hints.reason: Volcanoes are fire and lava; many are undersea or form ocean islands (Hawaii).
The Ring of Fire is the volcanic belt around the Pacific Ocean, reaching both words through one name.

best_available.why: The Pacific Ring of Fire is literally fire and ocean.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass; RING is the sharper one.

hints.reason: Blackbeard gives the pirate side; the fire side relies on the legend that he lit fuses in his beard, which few players know.
Pirate ships fire cannons; 'fire' is the verb for a cannon.

best_available.why: Verb route to fire plus the iconic pirate weapon.

pairs.pair_note: CANNON is strong; BEARD needs trivia.

hints.reason: Freddie Mercury fronts Queen; the fire side only works via Freddy Krueger's burn story, a different Freddy and a stretch.
Daenerys is the Dragon Queen of Game of Thrones, the Unburnt who walks through fire.

best_available.why: Queen and fire are both core to the character.

pairs.pair_note: DAENERYS is strong for anyone who knows the show; FREDDIE is one-sided.

hints.reason: A forge is fire, and the One Ring was forged in fire (Lord of the Rings).
Johnny Cash's 'Ring of Fire' names both targets.
The circus ring hosts fire-eaters and flaming hoops.

best_available.why: The song title is exactly the pair.

pairs.pair_note: Three good routes; CIRCUS is broadest, CASH is the neatest.

hints.reason: Firefighter is the compound; fighting robots (BattleBots, mech fighters) give the robot side.
The Terminator is the iconic robot; fire arrives via its gunfire and the molten-steel finale.

best_available.why: Compound on one side, a known genre on the other.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass at moderate strength; neither is a clean 2/2.

hints.reason: Flint is a rock used to strike fire.
Lava is molten rock, burning hot.
A volcano is a mountain of rock that erupts fire.

best_available.why: A rock whose purpose is making fire.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent pair; all three are strong.

hints.reason: Rose is the past tense of rise (inflection route); flames and smoke rise, and the phoenix rises from fire.
Fire is red and roses are red, a shared property both words own strongly.
Fiery passion and roses as symbols of passionate love share one mood.

best_available.why: The most immediate shared property for both words.

pairs.pair_note: RED is the safe serve; RISE is clever and depends on the verb reading of ROSE.

hints.reason: Meat is grilled over fire and seasoned or preserved with salt, but neither link is specific enough to point at the word.
Salt-curing is strong; fire-curing (over fire or smoke) is real but less familiar than smoke-curing.

best_available.why: Salt is nailed and the fire-cured route exists even if it is secondary.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Both hints are preservation-kitchen stretches; a smoke-based hint would serve this pair better.

hints.reason: Plato's cave and the cave-dweller scene both have a fire casting shadows on the wall.
Flames flicker and so do the shadows they throw, one shared verb.
Flames dance and shadows dance on the wall, a shared verb from the same firelit scene.

best_available.why: The verb belongs to both words equally.

pairs.pair_note: A pair with a natural shared scene; all three pass.

hints.reason: Shark attack is the compound; to open fire is to attack, and 'under fire' is a known phrase.
Jaws is the shark film, but nothing recognizable ties jaws to fire.

best_available.why: The only hint that reaches fire at all.

pairs.pair_note: Hard pair; ATTACK is adequate, JAWS is one-sided.

hints.reason: Snakes hiss, and a fire hisses when wet wood or water meets the flame.
Dragons breathe fire and are serpents in form (Chinese dragons especially).
A snake's forked tongue and 'tongues of flame' are both familiar.

best_available.why: Idiom on the fire side, anatomy on the snake side, both immediate.

pairs.pair_note: All pass; TONGUE is the neatest.

hints.reason: Fire ant is the compound; the spider side is only the shared creepy-crawly category.
A web is the spider's thing; there is no recognizable web route to fire.

best_available.why: At least the fire side is a real compound and ants sit next to spiders in a player's mind.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Both hints are one-sided; the pair needs a new hint (e.g. a venom/burn route).

hints.reason: Leap is a synonym of spring (the verb); flames leap, which supplies the fire side.
Pulling the trigger fires a gun; a trigger is spring-loaded.
Fire is hot and hot spring is a familiar compound.

best_available.why: Property on one side, compound on the other.

pairs.pair_note: HOT is the clear serve; LEAP works but is near-synonymous with one target.

hints.reason: Fire burns and stars are burning balls of gas.
Shooting star is the compound; shooting is firing a gun.
The sun is a star and a ball of fire.

best_available.why: Compound plus verb, both instant.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent pair; all three are strong.

hints.reason: Coal fuels a fire and the coal-fired steam train.
Steam train is the compound; steam is made by fire boiling water in the firebox.
Fire engine and train engine are both everyday compounds.

best_available.why: Two compounds, no explanation needed.

pairs.pair_note: All pass; ENGINE and COAL are the strongest.

hints.reason: A fire hydrant supplies water to fight fire.
A fire hose sprays water.
Water extinguishes fire; the verb binds the pair.

best_available.why: One object that is fire on the label and water inside.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent pair; all three are strong.

hints.reason: The witch's cauldron bubbles over a fire.
Salem is the witch-trial town, but the fire side depends on the misconception that Salem burned witches; they were hanged, so the route rests on a wrong fact.
Witches were burned at the stake; the phrase carries both words.

best_available.why: Burning at the stake is the shared story itself.

pairs.pair_note: Two strong hints; SALEM is failed on the factual rule even though many players would follow the misconception.

hints.reason: The brick house defeats the wolf in the Three Little Pigs; fire only arrives via the pot boiling in that house's fireplace or fire-bricks, both a hop too far.
A torch is fire, and torches keep wolves at bay or lead the torch-bearing mob hunting the werewolf.
Contains the target FIRE as a substring (rule failure).

best_available.why: Fire-to-ward-off-wolves is a recognizable wilderness scene.

pairs.pair_note: CAMPFIRE is a rule failure; TORCH is the only servable hint.

hints.reason: Ghosts float, and fish float (a fishing float, or the dead fish belly-up).
Ghosts are pale, but fish are not recognizably pale as a defining property.

best_available.why: Shared verb that fits both literally.

pairs.pair_note: FLOAT is good; PALE is one-sided.

hints.reason: A fish tank is a glass tank.
An aquarium is fish behind glass; essentially the same route as TANK.
A fishbowl is a glass bowl.

best_available.why: Fish tank is the most immediate compound.

pairs.pair_note: All three pass and are near-equivalent routes.

hints.reason: Omega-3 is the fish-oil nutrient marketed for heart health.
Salmon is a fish and the standard example of a heart-healthy food.
Fish oil is the compound and it is taken for the heart.

best_available.why: Omega-3 is the exact bridge between fish and heart.

pairs.pair_note: All three share the heart-healthy-fish route; OMEGA is the most pointed.

hints.reason: Bears eat honey and catch fish, the two foods everyone associates with them.
Honey glaze is the compound; honey-glazed salmon is a familiar dish reaching fish.

best_available.why: One animal whose two famous foods are the two targets.

pairs.pair_note: BEAR is excellent; GLAZE is a fair kitchen route.

hints.reason: Contains the target HORSE as a substring (rule failure).
Fish live in the sea, and sea + horse makes seahorse.
A mane is the horse's feature; no recognizable mane route reaches fish.

best_available.why: Habitat for fish plus the seahorse compound.

pairs.pair_note: SEA does the job; SEAHORSE is a rule failure and MANE is one-sided.

hints.reason: Ice fishing means cutting a hole in the ice to fish through.
Ice is frozen water and frozen fish is a supermarket staple.
Fish market is the compound; the fish there lie on ice.

best_available.why: The ice-fishing hole is one specific shared scene.

pairs.pair_note: All pass; HOLE and FROZEN are the strongest.

hints.reason: A fish hook is the compound and hooks are iron/metal.
Cast-iron skillet is the compound; frying fish in a skillet reaches fish.
An anchor is iron, but the fish side is only the generic sea theme or a fishing boat's anchor.

best_available.why: Compound on fish and an obvious metal object.

pairs.pair_note: HOOK and SKILLET serve; ANCHOR leans on iron alone.

hints.reason: Key West is the compound, but fish only arrives through Key West's fishing reputation, which is a second hop.
The Florida Keys give the key side; Florida's sport-fishing fame gives the fish side.

best_available.why: Geography route that at least evokes fishing directly.

pairs.pair_note: Both hints use the same Keys geography; FLORIDA reaches fish a little more naturally than WEST.

hints.reason: Mackerel is a fish and king mackerel is a well-known species.
King crab is the compound; crab sits with fish as seafood/the fish counter.
Contains both targets KING and FISH as substrings (rule failure).
Salmon is a fish and king salmon (Chinook) is a familiar name.

best_available.why: A more familiar fish than mackerel with the same king-species route.

pairs.pair_note: Three passes on the king-species route; KINGFISHER is a rule failure.

hints.reason: Fish have scales; knights wore scale armor (scale mail).
Armor is the knight's; fish only arrive via scales-as-armor, the same idea as SCALES but from the weaker side.

best_available.why: The shared-property route reaches both words directly.

pairs.pair_note: Hard pair; SCALES is the one usable hint.

hints.reason: Glow is light; glow-in-the-dark and bioluminescent fish (GloFish, deep-sea fish) reach fish.
A fishing lure is the compound; light lures fish and the anglerfish lures with its light.
An angler is a fisher and the anglerfish carries its own light.

best_available.why: Fishing and the lit anglerfish in one word.

pairs.pair_note: All pass; ANGLER is the most pointed.
